body:
Breaking Fractions Apart: 1. 1/5 + 1/5 + 1/5 + 1/5. 2. Examples: 1/6 + 4/6; 2/6 + 3/6; 1/6 + 1/6 + 3/6. 3. 5/8; 3/8 + 2/8 = 5/8. 4. 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 3/4. 5. 5 × 1/3; 1 2/3. 6. The pieces are still eighths: the denominator names the size of the pieces, which does not change. Five pieces of size 1/8 is 5/8.
Pizza Party Fractions: 1. 5/8. 2. 4/6 + 1/6 = 5/6 eaten, so 1/6 is left. 3. Examples: 3/8 + 4/8; 1/8 + 2/8 + 4/8; 1/8 + 6/8.
Mixed Numbers on the Trail: 1. 3 5/4 = 4 1/4 miles. 2. 3 1/8 = 2 9/8; 2 9/8 − 1 5/8 = 1 4/8 miles (also 1 1/2). 3. 13/5. 4. 2 3/4. 5. 4 × 2/3 = 8/3 = 2 2/3 cups. 6. 5 × 3/8 = 15/8 = 1 7/8 liters, between 1 and 2 liters. 7. 2 2/3.
Adding and Subtracting Fractions Check: 1. 7/10. 2. 2/12 (1/6 is also correct). 3. Examples: 1/8 + 2/8 + 3/8; 2/8 + 2/8 + 2/8. 4. 5/6 painted; 1/6 left. 5. 3 9/8 = 4 1/8. 6. 3 6/5 − 1 3/5 = 2 3/5. 7. 6/4 = 1 2/4 (also 1 1/2). 8. 3 × 3/4 = 9/4 = 2 1/4 cups. 9. Rory added the denominators; the pieces are still fifths, so 1/5 + 2/5 = 3/5.
Scoring tip: Grade 4 does not require simplest form, so 2/12 and 1 4/8 earn full accuracy credit. Score reasoning on the model or equation that shows the regrouping.
title: Answer key: Adding Fractions
